title: Five-round AES shifting-retracing boomerang distinguisher, corrected journal version

target.description: Five AES rounds with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted; single-key permutation distinguisher using encryption and inverse queries.

setting.reference_model: Uniformly random permutation on 128-bit blocks with consistent forward and inverse oracle access.
setting.key_relation: One unknown fixed key; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: 2^31.5 plaintexts varying bytes 0,5,10,15; filter ciphertext pairs with a fixed nonzero difference in bytes 0,7,10,13 and decrypt shifted counterparts
assumptions: The source's Section 4.1 explicitly makes the attack descriptions independent of the AES key schedule.
Costs and probability estimates follow the journal version's statistical assumptions; Appendix A.5 identifies rigorous probability analysis as further work.
The fixed 32-bit difference delta_L is nonzero. Page 28 footnote 9 explicitly withdraws the initial version's option of also accepting zero-difference ciphertext pairs.

time.note: Source's encryption-dominated estimate; hashing/filtering and expected decryptions are not an exact single term.

data.note: Source-reported dominant budget: 2^31.5 encryptions, plus an expected 2^31 decryptions from 2^30 surviving pairs. Not an exact total-query count.

memory.note: Source attributes dominant memory to storing the 2^31.5-block plaintext/ciphertext data set; implementation overhead is not itemized.

preprocessing.note: No separate preprocessing budget is reported.

success.description: After the nonzero-delta ciphertext-pair filter, the source assigns the plaintext predicate probabilities2^-28 for AES and2^-30 for a random permutation. Algorithm5 decides from counter>2 with expectations4 versus1. It supplies no distribution or numerical whole-game success; no Poisson law is inferred.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit; construction and parameter-specific defining passages, not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Source probability of the zero inverse-shifted-column plaintext predicate, conditional on the specified nonzero-delta ciphertext-pair filter.
Random-permutation predicate probability under the same filter; not the false-positive rate of the final counter>2 decision.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.28-29, Section 6.2, footnote 9 and Algorithm 5; p.15 Section 4.1.
evidence.interpretation: Uses the corrected nonzero-difference condition and distinguishes the headline data scale from the sum of encryption and decryption queries.

evidence.locator: Complete exact primary PDF1–42, all sections, formulas, tables, algorithms, appendices and references.
evidence.interpretation: Complete reading and source inventory; later-literature gates and finite controls separately recorded. No author attack code executed.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.28–29 Section6.2, footnote9 and Algorithm5 lines7–10.
evidence.interpretation: After the nonzero-delta ciphertext-pair filter, the source assigns the plaintext predicate probabilities2^-28 for AES and2^-30 for a random permutation. Algorithm5 decides from counter>2 with expectations4 versus1. It supplies no distribution or numerical whole-game success; no Poisson law is inferred.

limitations: The two expected counter values do not specify a numerical distinguishing advantage without a distributional analysis.
Costs use the source's dominant-term accounting; the procedure was not independently reproduced.
